body.p: This listing of claims will replace all prior versions, and listings, of claims in the application:

br.br:
1. (CURRENTLY AMENDED) An aircraft pylon fairing extending along a longitudinal axis, the aircraft pylon fairing comprising:a wall having at least two opposite flanks oriented respectively one on each side of said longitudinal axis,
a central interior cavity, the at least two opposite flanks meeting in a lower or upper part of said fairing,
a front transverse rib securely fixed to said wall and extending perpendicularly on each side of said longitudinal axis, said front transverse rib comprising a through opening configured to accept a peg of an exterior structure by push-fitting in a direction parallel to said longitudinal axis, and comprising two yokes each having bores along a longitudinalan axis oriented perpendicular to said longitudinal axis of the fairing and arranged facing a through opening in one of said opposing flanks, and
a rear transverse rib securely fixed to said wall and extending perpendicularly on each side of said longitudinal axis and comprising two yokes each having bores along a longitudinal an axis oriented perpendicular to said longitudinal axis of the fairing and arranged facing a through opening in one of said opposing flanks,
wherein the aircraft pylon fairing is a secondary structure which contributes to the aerodynamic performance for flight, and
wherein the exterior structure is a structure indispensable for flight.
2. (CURRENTLY AMENDED) An aircraft pylon fairing assembly comprising:the aircraft pylon fairing according tothe aircraft pylon fairing according to
four fixing elements which are configured to each be inserted into and held in position in [[a]] the bore of one of said yokes.
3. (ORIGINAL) An aircraft pylon comprising:the fairing assembly according tothe fairing assembly according to
an aircraft primary structure, said aircraft primary structure comprising a peg oriented along an axis parallel to the longitudinal axis of the fairing and configured to be inserted into said through opening of said front transverse rib, and four fittings which are respectively arranged in such a way as to each be inserted into one of said yokes and each having a through opening configured to be arranged facing said bore of said yoke and configured to receive a portion of one of said four fixing elements which is inserted into said bore of said yoke, said openings in the fittings which are configured to be inserted into the yokes of the front transverse rib of said fairing having an oblong shape extending in a direction perpendicular to the longitudinal axis of the fairing, and said openings in the fittings that are configured to be inserted into the yokes of the rear transverse rib of said fairing having an oblong shape extending along an axis parallel to said longitudinal axis of said fairing, or vice versa.
4. (CURRENTLY AMENDED) The aircraft pylon according to claim 3, wherein said openings in the fittings configured to be inserted into the yokes of the front transverse rib of said fairing have [[an]] the oblong shape extending in a direction perpendicular to the longitudinal axis of the fairing, andwherein said openings of the fittings configured to be inserted into the yokes of the rear transverse rib of said fairing have [[an]] the oblong shape extending along an axis parallel to said longitudinal axis of said fairing.
5. (ORIGINAL) The aircraft pylon according to claim 3, wherein said openings in the fittings configured to be inserted into the yokes of the front transverse rib of said
fairing have an oblong shape extending in a direction parallel to the longitudinal axis of the fairing, andwherein said openings of the fittings configured to be inserted into the yokes of the rear transverse rib of said fairing have an oblong shape extending along an axis perpendicular to said longitudinal axis of said fairing.
6. (ORIGINAL) The aircraft pylon according to claim 3, wherein the peg has a conical or frustoconical shape.
7. (ORIGINAL) The aircraft pylon according to claim 3, wherein the fixing elements are countersunk screws, andwherein all or part of each of said bores comprises an internal screw thread of a shape that complements a screw thread of said screws.
8. (CANCELLED)
9. (ORIGINAL) An aircraft comprising the aircraft pylon fairing according to claim 1.
10. (CURRENTLY AMENDED) A method for assembling the aircraft pylon according to claim 3, the method comprising:push-fitting the fairing onto the peg of the primary structure of [[an]] the aircraft pylon, then positioning said yokes of the fairing around the four fittings of the primary structure in such a way as to align said bores of said yokes with said oblong openings of said fittings, said fittings each being inserted into one of said yokes, and then inserting each of the four fixing elements into [[a]] the bore of a yoke into which a fitting has been inserted and into the oblong opening in said fitting so as to hold the fairing of said aircraft pylon in position on said primary structure in a statically determinate manner.
